lastCompletedStory.title: Remove dead-for-help guards in config, claude, and triage switch cases

nextStoryContext: US-001 was the only story in this PRD; all stories now pass. The `config` and `triage` cases had their dead `if (tail.includes('--help') ...) { write(...); return 0; }` blocks deleted cleanly (plain string[] tail, no type fallout). The `claude` case's parseClaudeArgs return type is a discriminated union ({help:true} | {help:false; forwardedArgs}), so its dead help-print block could not be deleted wholesale: an `if (parsed.help) return 0;` narrowing check remains (unreachable at runtime since the central --help guard already intercepts), needed purely to satisfy TS control-flow narrowing for `parsed.forwardedArgs`. Other switch cases (run, plan, spec, issue, next, review, ship, tag, dashboard, status, stop, drain, resume, retry-monitor, journal, patterns, suggestions) still carry the same class of now-dead-for-help guard per-case; this PRD did not touch them, so a future PRD targeting the same cleanup should expect the same discriminated-union-vs-plain-array split behavior seen here.
